 Through: Mr. Sumant Sudan, Advocate vice
 Mr. Vishal Sharma, Dsgi for R-1 to 5.
 Mrs. Monika Kohli, Sr. Aag for R-6 & 7.

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice M A Chowdhary, Judge
 Order

(08.11.2024)
01. Petitioner claiming to be owner of land measuring 3 Kanals comprising of Khasra Nos. 210 (02-00) & 216 (01- 00) situated at Phalyana, Tehsil & District Rajouri, which on requisition has been under the occupation of respondent Nos. 1 to 5 ever since the year 1961/62 and that the petitioner as owner of the land, had been receiving the settled rent for use of the land by the respondent Nos. 1 to 5, from the Collectorate.
02. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that with the coming into effect of the Jammu &
Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019 on 31.08.2019, the State of Jammu and Kashmir was organized into two Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, and in terms of Section 95(2) of the aforesaid Act, all the laws mentioned in the 5th Schedule applicable to the existing State of Jammu & Kashmir, immediately before the appointed day were made applicable in the manner provided in the 5th Schedule; that the Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1968 (State Act),
was mentioned at serial no. 133 in TABLE-3 of 5th Schedule which contained the enactments which stood repealed correspondingly Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1952 (Central Act) was made applicable.

sentences.text:
occupying the property under occupation is either to be acquired in view of the law applicable or its possession is to be handed over to the owner.
03.

It has been submitted that after the expiry of 17 years and in view of constitutional changes, the period of limitation was held to be extendable by one year which also expired on 31st October, 2020 and thereafter the land owned by the petitioner has been under the occupation of the respondents No. 1 to 5, without sanction of law.

It was prayed that the respondents be directed either to acquire or hand over the possession to the petitioner as owner of the land and damages for the period of use and occupation of the land after 31st October, 2020, be also directed to be paid.

06. Notices waived by Mr. Sumant Sudan, assisting counsel vice Mr. Vishal Sharma, learned DSGI,
on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 to 5 and Mrs. Monika Kohli, learned Senior AAG on behalf of the respondents No. 6 & 7.
Respondents are directed to file reply/objections within a period of four weeks.

07. Meanwhile, it is provided that future deposit of the rent, if any, in the Account of the petitioner as rental compensation of the land, shall not be any impediment to the claims of the petitioner made in this petition.

08. CM No. 6473/2024 is, accordingly, disposed of.
09. List on 27.12.2024.
(M A CHOWDHARY) JUDGE JAMMU 08.11.2024
